topic: What if you could see one minute ahead?
title: WHAT IF YOU COULD
GLIMPSE ONE MINUTE AHEAD?

power.rule: see exactly sixty seconds into the future, any time you want
power.look: a cyan selection box with marching ants draws around the future moment; a GLIMPSE chip pulses; the frame holds a ghost image of what's coming

script.text: Coffee tips. Glimpse. You catch it.
Bus pulls off. Glimpse. You make it.
Friend speaks. Glimpse. You said it first.
What if you could glimpse one minute ahead?

script.beat: 4 the turn: the cost, one real fact
script.text: Your brain runs on twenty watts. One minute of future simulation needs twelve hundred — a space heater in your skull. That's real.
So what happens when the power fails?

science.claim: Your brain runs on twenty watts. One minute of future simulation needs twelve hundred watts — a space heater in your skull.
science.working: The human brain consumes about 20 W at rest (20% of ~100 W basal metabolic rate; Raichle & Gusnard, 2002). Simulating 60 seconds of conscious experience in 1 second of real time (parallel future simulation) requires 60× the metabolic power: 20 W × 60 = 1,200 W. A typical portable space heater draws 1,500 W, so 1,200 W is 'a space heater in your skull.'
science.source: Raichle & Gusnard, 'Appraising the brain's energy budget,' PNAS 2002 (brain ~20 W); typical space heater 1,500 W
